title: Part Thirty-One: Tithe, Sabbath and Obedience: Two Economies of the Sacred

sections.brief: Tithe from gift to law to tax: Hebrew Levitical tithe; early voluntary giving (link vt20); Caesarius of Arles theory (Shuler 2012); Tours 567, Mâcon 585 (excommunication), Herstal March 779 (royal enforcement), four-way division; England pre-Conquest, Lateran III 1179, Saladin tithe, Lateran IV tithes before taxes; annates (1305, 1319, servitia), Peter's Pence (Canute 1031, ended 1534, Saepe venerabilis 1871), indulgences (Albrecht, Fugger 20,000 guilders, bull 31 March 1515, Tetzel 1517; Trent 1563, Pius V 1567); France August 1789, England 1836/1936/1977; today CIC 222, 1260-1263, CCC 2043; otto per mille and German Kirchensteuer (€6.751bn 2025). Figures: time (tithe), money (five revenue streams)

Sunday and the law of obligation: Justin and Didache as custom; Elvira canon 21 (three Sundays); Constantine 321 (link vt21); Laodicea, Apostolic Constitutions; Agde 506 (Caesarius; communion at Christmas, Easter, Pentecost); Orléans 538; Lateran IV 1215 annual confession and Easter communion under excommunication and loss of burial; CIC 1246-1247, CCC 2181 'grave sin', 2042-2043 precepts, 2188 legal holidays; German Mass attendance 6.8% (2025); leaving: canon 1364, Theodosian apostasy laws, German bishops' decree Sept 2012 and Leipzig ruling 26 Sept 2012 (Zapp); Gospel of Mary (Mattison), Thomas 14 and 27, Philip on freedom, Ptolemy keeps Decalogue, Pistis Sophia code. Figures: time (obligation), compare (rules in two records)

Synthesis: eight-row comparison (access, intermediary, payment, obligation, authority, women, text, sanction for leaving), each cell sourced; exceptions both ways (Valentinians in churches, Marcion's money returned, Marcus allegation, Manichaean Hearers, Cathar bishops/perfecti working as weavers, early church poor relief); Weber's office charisma and Pagels as attributed scholarly arguments; labelled interpretation (appropriation, suppression, occultation, recovery; 'unmediated access threatens a mediated institution'); counter-readings (Metzger canon as recognition, Valentinian elitism and Pagels' critics, heresiologists' pastoral motive, every lasting group built offices). Figures: compare
